skill.name: firefox-browser
skill.description: Control Firefox browser sessions with existing user logins for page inspection, navigation, form entry, and screenshots.
skill.summary: Automate live Firefox tabs with authenticated browser context and page interaction commands.
skill.author: 1jehuang

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown formatting around documented commands, not dynamic Ruby or shell substitution. Confirmed risks remain because the skill starts Firefox as a background process, can capture authenticated page screenshots, and intentionally controls the user logged-in browser session. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Document process lifetime, prefer attaching to an existing browser, and provide a cleanup command after tasks finish.
Require explicit user confirmation before reading private pages, handling authentication, purchases, or changing account settings.
Gate screenshots behind user approval and warn when the active page may contain private data.
Constrain instructions to the browser CLI and avoid unrelated shell command examples.

content.value_statement: Browser tasks often need access to pages that already trust the user's Firefox profile. This skill guides agents to inspect tabs, navigate pages, fill forms, and capture page state.
actual_capabilities: Start or connect to Firefox and verify bridge connectivity with browser ping.
List, create, switch, and manage Firefox tabs or isolated sessions.
Navigate to URLs and extract page content as text, HTML, or annotated interactables.
Click elements, type into inputs, and fill forms using selectors or visible text.
Capture visible browser page screenshots to a PNG file.
Use fork, tryUntil, and parallel workflows for uncertain or multi-page tasks.
limitations: Requires Firefox, the bridge, and the browser command to be installed and running.
Uses the user's active browser profile, so sensitive sessions require explicit oversight.
Cannot bypass site permissions, authentication requirements, CAPTCHAs, or anti-automation controls.
Commands can change live pages, forms, and account state if used without care.

use_cases.title: Inspect Authenticated Web Apps
use_cases.description: Review visible pages and controls in a logged-in Firefox session while preserving the user browser context.

use_cases.title: Automate Repetitive Form Work
use_cases.description: Fill known fields, wait for required elements, and pause before submitting important forms.

use_cases.title: Compare Pages Across Sites
use_cases.description: Open multiple URLs in isolated tabs and compare visible text, prices, availability, or page states.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open https://example.com in a new Firefox session. Read the page in annotated format and summarize the main visible content.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form With Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the form page I provide, inspect interactable fields, fill the requested values, and stop before submitting for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Product Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use parallel sessions for these product URLs, collect visible prices and availability, and report differences without making purchases.

prompt_templates.title: Test Multiple Auth Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Fork the current login page into Google and email authentication paths, document which path succeeds, and close unused forks.

output_examples.output: The skill opens a dedicated tab, reads annotated content, lists visible controls, and reports the current dashboard status.

output_examples.input: Fill a support request form with approved details.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies fields, enters approved values, notes missing required information, and waits before final submission.
The skill uses separate sessions, extracts price and stock text, and returns a concise comparison.

best_practices: Start with a new session or explicit tabId for each task.
Review annotated content before clicking, typing, or submitting forms.
Ask for user approval before actions involving accounts, purchases, or private data.
anti_patterns: Do not operate on an active personal tab without confirming the target tab.
Do not capture screenshots of sensitive pages unless the user asks for them.
Do not submit forms, purchase items, or change account settings without approval.

faq.question: Does this use my real Firefox profile?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls the user's Firefox browser, including existing logins and cookies.

faq.question: Does it run a headless browser?
faq.answer: No. It uses the actual Firefox browser session through a local bridge.

faq.question: Can it work with login pages?
faq.answer: It can detect authentication pages and request approval, but it cannot bypass authentication.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It can capture the visible browser page as a PNG, so treat screenshots as sensitive.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Firefox, the bridge, and the browser command must be installed and reachable.

faq.question: Is it safe for private accounts?
faq.answer: Use it with explicit oversight because it can view and interact with authenticated pages.
